notes: Prove the public polarity of the Congo Fliptronic cabinet flipper-button optos (public 112 lower right, 114 lower left, 118 upper left, 116 not used) on GEN_WPC95. Direct switch writes only, so PinMAME keyboard handling, the flipper-key path, and the built-in simulator stay off. Four balls are presented on the normalized trough optos (public 32-35), the fresh-NVRAM notice is cleared with one service Escape, the coin door is closed, credits are added through coin switch 1 and a game is started; once the trough eject (public solenoid 9) proves a game is running, each button address (112 lower right, 114 lower left, then 118 upper left, the not-used 116 upper right position, and 115, the upper right end-of-stroke position PinMAME does not synthesize) is held at public level 1 and then released while the flipper outputs 35/36 and 45-48 are recorded. The driver declares FLIP_SOL(FLIP_L | FLIP_UL), so 35/36 and 45-48 carry the ROM's own Fliptronic flipper-coil writes rather than PinMAME's synthetic button-derived states. This scenario proves emulator-facing polarity and causality only, not physical opto construction or coil force.
